main_issue: Who should pay for juices/soft drinks for the housewarming after the shared drinks fund was spent entirely on alcohol

A-B.evidence: B asks about juices (2) and A agrees (3); B proposes everyone chip in (4), later accepts A already put in extra (14), which A's complaint (13) prompted.

A-C.evidence: C objects to paying more from the fund (5), but C's final plan (17) says A already put in extra and is covered, which fits A's wish (13).

A-D.evidence: D says she is uncomfortable that the money went on alcohol (6) and A concedes the mistake (7), but D then backs a plan that makes drinkers pay (12) and A objects to paying again (13).

B-C.evidence: C rejects B's chip-in (5) and split (9); B moves to include C and drinkers in the split (14); C still objects to D paying and B asks for C's plan (15-17); B stays unconvinced.

B-D.evidence: B proposed that B and D buy juices and split (8), then B proposed D pay as part of the three-way split (14), while D endorsed C's drinkers-pay approach (12).

C-D.evidence: D says 'He's got a point' (6) and 'That sounds fair' (12); C defends D as a non-drinker who should not pay (15, 17).
